subtitle: How frontier kings and a copper plate marked the edge of an empire

panels.shot: dramatic split-composition, one half showing Nagabhata I on a rampart, the other Avanijanashraya before a scribe etching a plate
panels.action: Nagabhata I stands in armor atop a Rajasthan fort wall gazing west over arid plains as storm clouds gather, while Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin in Gujarat courtly dress watches a Brahmin scribe incise a gleaming copper plate on a low desk.

dialogue.text: A copper plate in Navsari, a praise-song in Gwalior, and Arab chronicles in Baghdad together trace how Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya held the eastern edge of the Caliph’s advance.

i18n.hi: नवसारी का ताम्रपट्ट, ग्वालियर की प्रशंसा-शिला और बगदाद की अरब कथाएँ मिलकर दिखाती हैं कैसे नागभट्ट और अवनिजनाश्रय ने ख़लीफ़ा की बढ़त को पूरब में थाम दिया।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Indus and Sindh, with faint arrows pushing eastward
panels.action: The camera floats high above the Indus valley showing the river curling through Sindh, small Arab garrison towns dotting its banks, with ghostly arrow-like trails hinting at routes pushing toward Rajasthan, Malwa and Gujarat.

dialogue.text: After Sindh fell to the armies of the Umayyad caliphs, their governors looked east. Beyond the Indus lay Malwa, Rajasthan, and the rich ports of Gujarat.

i18n.hi: सिंध उमय्यद ख़लीफ़ाओं के हाथ गिरा तो उनके सूबेदारों की नज़र पूरब पर गई। सिंध के पार थे मालवा, राजस्थान और गुजरात के मालदार बंदरगाह।

panels.shot: interior, dim Abbasid court archival hall with a scholar reading
panels.action: An Arab scholar in a simple robe sits under a lamp in an Abbasid-era library, unrolling a parchment as shelves of bound volumes fade into darkness behind him.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Ahmad al-Baladhuri would write in Baghdad of raids launched from Sindh, naming towns and rivers, but not of any lasting conquest beyond that frontier.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, अहमद अल-बलाज़ुरी बगदाद में लिखता है कि सिंध से कितने हमले चले, कितने कस्बे–नदियाँ लुटीं, पर उस सरहद के आगे किसी टिकाऊ फ़तह का ज़िक्र नहीं करता।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nagabhata I in a frontier fort, map before him
panels.action: Nagabhata I, in mail and turbaned helmet, stands over a rough map scratched on a wooden board, walls of a rugged Rajasthan hill-fort rising around him and weary scouts reporting at his side.

dialogue.text: On this frontier, new powers stirred. One was Nagabhata, first of the Gurjara-Pratiharas, holding lines in Rajasthan and Malwa as Arab probes searched for weak seams.

i18n.hi: यहीं सरहद पर नई ताक़तें उठीं। एक था नागभट्ट, गुरजर-प्रतिहारों का पहला, जो राजस्थान-मालवा में मोर्चे सँभाले हुए था, जबकि अरब टोह दस्ते कमज़ोर दरारें खोज रहे थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Avanijanashraya in a Gujarat coastal town, ships behind
panels.action: Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin, in elegant Chalukya-feudatory attire, stands on a raised platform in a bustling Gujarat port near Navsari, palm trees and masts of sea-going ships visible beyond the town walls.

dialogue.text: Farther south-west in Gujarat, Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin served as a Chalukya feudatory. His task: guard the coastal routes, where Arab fleets and columns could converge.

i18n.hi: और दक्षिण-पश्चिम में, गुजरात में, अवनिजनाश्रय पुलकेशिन चालुक्य सामंत के रूप में तैनात था। उसका काम था समुद्री राहों की रखवाली, जहाँ अरब बेड़े और जथ्थे मिल सकते थे।

panels.shot: low wide shot of an Arab column crossing a semi-arid plain
panels.action: An Arab military column in mail and helmets rides and marches across a semi-arid landscape, banners fluttering, with a distant Indian fort silhouetted on a hill ahead.

dialogue.text: Baladhuri’s pages recall Arab commanders pushing toward the lands of the ‘Rur’ and beyond, leading contingents from Sindh into the plains east and south of the desert.

i18n.hi: बलाज़ुरी के पन्ने बताते हैं अरब सेनापति ‘रूर’ और आगे की धरती की ओर धकेलते हैं, सिंध से निकली टुकड़ियाँ रेगिस्तान के पूरब और दक्षिण के मैदानी इलाकों तक ले जाते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on Nagabhata I’s face, lit by firelight, thoughtful
panels.action: Nagabhata I’s weathered face fills the frame in flickering firelight as he listens to a messenger, jaw tight, the sounds of camp and distant drums blurred behind him.

dialogue.text: We do not have Nagabhata’s own words. What we have are later praises carved in stone, remembering how he faced what one inscription would call an ‘invincible mleccha army’.

i18n.hi: नागभट्ट के अपने शब्द हमारे पास नहीं। हमारे पास हैं बाद की शिलालेख स्तुतियाँ, जहाँ लिखा है कि उसने एक ‘अजेय म्लेच्छ सेना’ का सामना किया।

panels.shot: close-up of hands carving letters into stone at Gwalior
panels.action: Hands of a stone carver patiently chisel sharp Nagari letters into a monumental slab, while a priest and a court poet supervise in a hall that hints at Gwalior’s later Pratihara glory.

dialogue.text: In Gwalior, much later, Mihira Bhoja’s panegyrist would recall Nagabhata as the one who repulsed that army. Epigraphers call it the Gwalior prashasti, and treat it as dynastic memory.

i18n.hi: बहुत बाद में ग्वालियर में, मिहिर भोज के कवि ने नागभट्ट को उसी सेना को धकेलने वाला नायक कहा। इसे आज विद्वान ग्वालियर प्रशस्ति कहते हैं, और राजवंशी स्मृति मानते हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Nagabhata I riding out of a fort gate with cavalry
panels.action: Nagabhata I rides out through a massive fort gateway at the head of armoured cavalry, dust rising around their horses as archers and spearmen form up on the rocky slope.

dialogue.text: The inscription gives no date, no named battlefield, only boast and outcome. But between those lines, historians see a series of clashes that hardened a frontier across Rajasthan and Malwa.

i18n.hi: इस शिलालेख में न तारीख़ है, न किसी रणभूमि का नाम, बस शेखी और नतीजा। मगर इन्हीं पंक्तियों के बीच इतिहासकार राजस्थान-मालवा भर में फैली कई झड़पें देखते हैं, जिनसे सरहद सख़्त हुई।

panels.shot: long shot of Navsari countryside, Arab and Indian forces facing each other
panels.action: Across flat fields near a river, an Arab host in tight formation faces a mixed Indian army with elephant line and cavalry, Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin visible near the center beneath a parasol.

dialogue.text: In Gujarat, one engagement came into sharper focus. There, near Navsari, an army from Sindh advanced. Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin met them, and this time, his scribes recorded the victory in copper.

i18n.hi: गुजरात में एक मुठभेड़ साफ़ दिखती है। नवसारी के पास सिंध से आई एक सेना बढ़ी। अवनिजनाश्रय पुलकेशिन उससे भिड़ा, और इस बार उसके लेखकों ने जीत तांबे पर खुदवा दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Avanijanashraya commanding, arm raised, elephants ahead
panels.action: Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin stands atop a war elephant, arm outstretched giving orders as lines of elephants and foot soldiers brace, Arab riders visible in the hazy distance.

dialogue.speaker: nagabhata_i_and_avanijanashraya_pulakeshin
dialogue.text: Steady the line. Let them feel the weight of this land.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति मज़बूत रखो। इन्हें इस धरती का भार महसूस होने दो।

panels.shot: medium shot of Avanijanashraya commanding, arm raised, elephants ahead
panels.action: Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin stands atop a war elephant, arm outstretched giving orders as lines of elephants and foot soldiers brace, Arab riders visible in the hazy distance.

dialogue.speaker: nagabhata_i_and_avanijanashraya_pulakeshin
dialogue.text: Steady the line. Let them feel the weight of this land.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति मज़बूत रखो। इन्हें इस धरती का भार महसूस होने दो।

panels.shot: close-up on the Navsari copper plate being held up to the light
panels.action: A Brahmin official lifts the freshly inscribed Navsari copper plate toward the light, rows of precise characters catching the glow, Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin’s figure blurred behind.

dialogue.text: Dated around 745 CE, the Navsari plate names him Avanijanashraya, protector of earth, and declares that he defeated a mleccha army. Unlike legend, this document stands almost beside the event.

i18n.hi: लगभग ७४५ ई. का नवसारी ताम्रपट्ट उसे ‘अवनिजनाश्रय’ – धरती का रक्षक – कहता है, और घोषित करता है कि उसने म्लेच्छ सेना को हराया। कथा से अलग, यह दस्तावेज़ घटना के लगभग साथ खड़ा है।

panels.shot: interior of a Chalukya court, ministers listening to reading of the plate
panels.action: In a Chalukya hall, Avanijanashraya sits modestly as a court reader recites from the copper plate, ministers and nobles listening in still attention, pillars carved with simple motifs around them.

dialogue.text: The plate credits him as a loyal feudatory of his Chalukya overlord. Its purpose was land grant and royal favour, yet in its flourish it preserves a frontier clash with extraordinary clarity.

i18n.hi: पट्ट उसे अपने चालुक्य स्वामी का वफ़ादार सामंत बताता है। असल मक़सद था ज़मीन दान और शाही कृपा, पर उसकी अलंकारिक पंक्तियों में सरहद की वह भिड़ंत असाधारण साफ़ी से बची रही।

panels.shot: map shot, slow zoom on a line arching from Sindh, bending, then stopping
panels.action: A stylized map appears, showing arrows from Sindh arcing into Rajasthan, Malwa and Gujarat, then bending back, with subtle fort icons marking regional centers held by local rulers.

dialogue.text: Modern histories, reading Arabic texts alongside these plates, see not one single ‘Battle of Rajasthan’, but a frontier series. Raids pressed in, met fort by fort, and then their momentum ebbed.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार, अरब ग्रंथों को इन ताम्रपट्टों के साथ पढ़कर, कोई एक ‘राजस्थान का महायुद्ध’ नहीं देखते, बल्कि एक सरहदी शृंखला। हमले आते रहे, हर क़िले पर टकराए, और फिर उनकी रफ़्तार टूट गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya shown separately, both in thoughtful repose
panels.action: In a split frame, Nagabhata I leans against the battlement of a Malwa fort at dusk, while Avanijanashraya stands beneath a tree near a Gujarat shrine, both in quiet reflection after campaign.

dialogue.text: For the caliphal governors in Sindh, these setbacks, distance, and other priorities made deep conquest eastward unattractive. For Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya, they were chances to consolidate.

i18n.hi: सिंध के ख़लीफ़ी सूबेदारों के लिए ये नाकामियाँ, दूरी और दूसरे मोर्चे, पूरब में गहरी फ़तह को बेकार सौदा बना देती हैं। नागभट्ट और अवनिजनाश्रय के लिए यही मौके थे अपनी पकड़ जमाने के।

panels.shot: wide view of a Pratihara court, anachronistic hint of later power
panels.action: A later Pratihara court scene shows a king presiding over an orderly hall, banners and musicians arranged with ceremony, suggesting the matured power that grew from frontier strongholds.

dialogue.text: Out of Nagabhata’s era grew the Gurjara-Pratihara kingdom, one of north India’s great powers. Its poets anchored their claim not only in lineage, but in that remembered stand against the mlecchas.

i18n.hi: नागभट्ट के ज़माने से ही उभरता है गुरजर-प्रतिहार राज्य, उत्तर भारत की बड़ी ताक़तों में एक। उनके कवि अपना हक़ सिर्फ़ वंश पर नहीं, उस म्लेच्छ-विरोधी डटकर लड़ाई पर भी टिकाते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a bard reciting before Rajput listeners, with shadowy imagery of Bappa Rawal behind
panels.action: A medieval bard stands before Rajput nobles, gesturing as he sings, while behind him in shadowy imagination appears the figure of Bappa Rawal leading warriors against foreign foes.

dialogue.text: Much later, songs in Rajasthan would place names like Bappa Rawal into these struggles, weaving legend onto history. Inscriptions, however, keep their silence on him for this frontier.

i18n.hi: काफ़ी बाद में, राजस्थान की लोक-कथाएँ बप्पा रावल जैसे नाम इन्हीं संघर्षों में डाल देती हैं, इतिहास पर लोक-गाथा की बुनावट चढ़ा देती हैं। पर शिलालेख इस सरहद पर उसके बारे में चुप रहते हैं।

panels.shot: modern historian at a desk with books, copper plate facsimile, and Arabic text
panels.action: A modern historian sits at a cluttered desk, Navsari plate facsimile, photographs of the Gwalior inscription, and a printed Arabic text of Futuh al-Buldan laid side by side under a reading lamp.

dialogue.text: Today, scholars lay these fragments together: Arabic narratives, copper grants, stone eulogies. Where they agree, we glimpse the frontier; where they differ, we see how memory shapes power.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान इन टुकड़ों को जोड़ते हैं – अरबी बयान, ताम्रपत्र अनुदान, पत्थर पर प्रशंसाएँ। जहाँ सब मिलते हैं, वहाँ सरहद झलकती है; जहाँ अलग होते हैं, वहाँ दिखता है कि यादें सत्ता को कैसे गढ़ती हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot over the Rajasthan-Gujarat landscape at sunrise, ghostly outlines of forts and routes
panels.action: From high above at sunrise, the camera drifts over the scrublands and river valleys of Rajasthan, Malwa and Gujarat, faint silhouettes of forts, caravan tracks, and coastal towns glowing in soft light.

dialogue.text: The Arab advance east of the Indus slowed not at a single miracle battle, but along a line of local defenders like Nagabhata and Avanijanashraya, whose quiet victories still mark where empires stopped.

i18n.hi: सिंध के पार अरब बढ़त किसी एक चमत्कारी युद्ध से नहीं, बल्कि ऐसे ही स्थानीय रक्षकों – नागभट्ट, अवनिजनाश्रय – की कतार से धीमी पड़ी, जिनकी खामोश जीतें आज भी दिखाती हैं कि साम्राज्य कहाँ रुक गए।

title_i18n.en: The Copper Plate That Checked the Arab Advance
title_i18n.hi: अरबों की बढ़त रोकने वाली ताम्रपट्ट कथा

subtitle_i18n.en: How frontier kings and a copper plate marked the edge of an empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: सीमा के राजा और एक ताम्रपट्ट – साम्राज्य की हद यहीं तक
